Each table and chair component is a separate object rather than a parented assembly: original_inspection/capture/original/object_inventory.jsonl:10-75 and build.py:45-74.
spatial_and_orientation_analysis: The reference and delivered image both depict a centered two-pane window over parallel desk rows and white wheeled chairs. The candidate is much more frontal and symmetric: the back-wall top and gray region above it are visible, the right foreground chair is largely clipped, and the more oblique reference has prominent right wall and two visible lamps. Camera pose, room extent and layout jointly confound these differences. Evidence: reference image, executions/blender_1795841702424816251/artifacts/final.png, final_source/build.py:19-23,45-50,74-87.

Chair backs indicate a broad facing direction toward desks, but some chairs are occluded or clipped, and symmetric bases do not determine exact orientation. The implementation varies two chair angles while most are zero: build.py:51-55,74. Absolute scale and hidden layout cannot be inferred from a single view; no aligned world-space errors are asserted.
appearance_and_resource_analysis: The reference has faint wall hexagons, dark tables and warm wall light pools. The delivered image has a faint hexagonal pattern and light walls but appears flatter, with only one obvious lamp at the right and no similarly prominent paired wall-light pools. Reference image and executions/blender_1795841702424816251/artifacts/final.png; build.py:24-38,75-85.

The floor material 'Pale stone floor' is a uniform Principled material assigned to 'Floor'; 'Warm ivory walls', 'Charcoal grey tabletops' and 'White molded chair plastic' are similarly assigned. Source sets base color and roughness rather than constructing an image or noise mapping: final_source/build.py:6-10,19-22,45-48,65-69. Extracted detailed_state.json:81085-81355 records the floor material and its Principled BSDF output connection. The hex pattern is a separate beveled curve in world coordinates, not a mapped image: build.py:24-38. No image texture, coordinate mapping or packed texture is authored by the delivered source; original_inspection/capture/original/summary.json:3-7 reports no missing external images. No full-reference image plane is evidenced.

Independent white-world images are evaluator products, not student tests; they retain camera, geometry and material confounds and do not establish a benefit: input_index.json:24-33; independent_evaluation/common_light/capture/common_light.png; reference_gt/common_light/capture/common_light.png.
geometry_analysis: Window panes are thin colored boxes mounted in front of a solid back wall rather than evidence of a cut opening; their material is named glass but the source creates an opaque default Principled shader: final_source/build.py:6-8,21,40-43. Chair backs are custom meshes with solidify and subdivision, seats and wheels are flattened spheres, and spokes are cylinders: build.py:51-74.

The model's explicit wheel centers and radii nominally place wheel bottoms at floor height, and table legs span to floor level, but nominal bounds cannot establish physical contact, stability, connectivity or absence of intersections: build.py:20,45-48,70-73; original_inspection/capture/original/object_inventory.jsonl:1,11,62-72. Evaluator broad-phase overlap count 275 is a candidate count, not confirmed collisions: original_inspection/capture/original/summary.json:8-16.
